newsitem.title: UK: Saatchi & Saatchi launches Carlsberg ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Saatchi & Saatchi launches Carlsberg ad campaign.

text.p: Saatchi & Saatchi on Wednesday said it would launch a six million pound ($9.8 million) advertising campaign for Carlsberg lager designed to position the beer as a contemporary brand.

The ad, which will break on Friday, is Saatchi & Saatchi's first advert for Carlsberg since the agency merged with K Advertising earlier this year. K Advertising originally handled the Carlsberg account.
Saatchi & Saatchi is owned by Cordiant Plc.

The advert draws on the recent popularity of science fiction films and features an alien invasion of Carlsberg's Copenhagen brewery, which prompts world leaders from the White House, Downing Street and the Kremlin to unite in an offensive against the enemy.

David Suchet, best-known as Agatha Christie's Hercule Poirot in the British television series, does the voiceover for the ad, which revives the Carlsberg strapline, "Probably the best lager in the world." Carlsberg introduced the strapline in 1974 with Orson Welles.

Saatchi & Saatchi also said it would break a cinema advert for Head & Shoulders dandruff shampoo on Friday alongside the science fiction film "Men In Black". The advert shows the "Men In Black" wardrobes of black suits and ties supplemented with bottles of the shampoo with the strapline: "Head and Shoulders. Keeping the Men In Black in black."
